To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

part of the deleterious effect of glucocorticoids on bone formation is due to the induction of ER stress and apoptosis of osteoblastic cells and that this effect is alleviated by inhibition of eIF-2α dephosporylation.

glucocorticoids induce apoptosis of osteoblastic cells by inducing endoplasmic-reticulum stress, and that inhibiting the dephosphorylating of eIF2a protects from the pro-apoptosis and anti-mineralization effects of glucocorticoids on osteoblastic and osteocyte cells in vitro and in bone in vivo.
part of the deleterious actions of glucocorticoids on the skeleton is mediated through induction of ER stress, and inhibition of eIF-2α dephosporylation prevents osteoblast and bone loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which glucocorticoid (GC)-induced apoptosis of osteocytes and osteoblasts is mediated and how it may be prevented.
the mechanisms by which GC induces osteoblast and bone cell death.
the effects of glucocorticoids on osteoblast and/or osteocyte viability, function, and apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GC induced apoptosis of osteoblastic cells in vitro and in bone of female mice in vivo is associated with induction of ROS/oxidative stress and ER stress.
GC-induced ER stress and subsequent osteoblast and/or osteocyte apoptosis is prevented in vitro and in female mice by inhibiting eIF2α phosphorylation.
GC induced osteoblast and/or osteocyte apoptosis and bone loss are due to ER stress, and this is prevented by inhibition of eIF-2α dephophorylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ER stress is a mechanism by which GCs induce apoptosis of osteoblastic cells and inhibition of dephosphorylated eIF2α prevents GC-induced osteoblastic cell death.

glucocorticoid-induced apoptosis of osteocytes and osteoblasts is mediated in part through induction of ER stress, and inhibition of eIF-2α dephophorylation prevents this apoptosis and the associated bone loss.

ER stress is a major mechanism by which GCs induce apoptosis of osteoblastic cells and inhibition of eIF 2α dephophorylation by salubrinal protects against GC-induced apoptosis and the deleterious actions of GC on the osteoblastic cells in vitro and in the skeleton in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

GC-induced ER stress is an important mechanism of osteoblast and/or osteocyte apoptosis, and that inhibition eIF2α phosphatase activity can protect from the deleterous effect of GC on osteocytic and osteoblastic cells.
GC-induced osteoblast/osteocyte death and bone loss is mediated in part through ER stress.

glucocorticoids induce endoplasmic (ER) stress, which is alleviated by eIF2a phosphorylation, and that inhibition or prevention of eIF2a dephosphoryation prevents apoptosis of osteoblastic cells and protects against the deleterious actions of GCs on the skeleton.
